note: Source of the Code size estimator (tools/code_size.py, tools/render_code_size.py). Every build names the rows it reads: data/results/<board>.csv (test, variant), a memory-breakdown.json build, or a table copied from a named README (manual). Sizes are never typed here; the module reads them and refuses a row that is not measured. 'none' lists the Builds projects with no build size on record; each gets the same reason unless it names its own.
ram_total_note: Where a row states its own SRAM total the row wins. Otherwise: CC2340R5 36,864 B and CC2755P10 165,888 B (boards.csv KB x 1024), CC1354P10 262,144 B SRAM (its rows state it), ESP32-C6 452,112 B static DIRAM (its rows state it), CC35X1 520,783 B main DRAM (the ESPHome row: 445,030 B used plus 75,753 B free; the 128 kB TCM is separate).

cc35x1|wifi-esphome-api.note: RAM is the main DRAM region (445,030 B used, 75,753 B free). The 128 kB TCM is separate, 42,280 B used.

cc35x1|freertos.note: RAM is the main DRAM region only (2,048 B used). The program also uses 35,788 B of the TCM, a separate 128 kB region.

cc35x1|matter-thermostat-ram.note: RAM is the Matter image's two regions added: TCM 127.4 kB of 128 kB and main data RAM 443.9 kB of 509 kB, from the experiment's region table (to 0.1 kB). The row's 593,248 B is data plus bss from arm-none-eabi-size, which counts a different way. The FreeRTOS heap (324 kB) is inside the main data RAM. The TCM is the tight region: the thermostat alone leaves about 0.6 kB of it.

flash_total_note: Flash totals are the chip's flash from data/boards.csv, except where the row names a smaller region: an update slot (CC2340R5 OTA rows), FLASH_NON_SECURE (CC35X1 ESPHome row), the app partition (ESP32-C6 ESPHome rows) or the one bank the linker uses (AM13E230, FLASH_BANK0, 256 kB).

ram_basis.cc35x1: RAM is the main DRAM region, FreeRTOS heap included; the 128 kB TCM is separate.
ram_basis.esp32c6: RAM is static data only (DIRAM); heap use at run time is extra.

flash_basis.esp32c6: Flash is the 8 MB module flash. Two sibling ESPHome rows state a 3,932,160 B app partition, so the real limit for an app is likely smaller.
flash_basis.cc35x1: Flash is the 8 MB external flash chip. The ESPHome row on this chip names a 2,751,488 B FLASH_NON_SECURE region for the application, so the limit for a larger image may be smaller.

cc2340r5-ble-dual.layout: Dual image on the chip. The app runs the update service and receives the new image into a second slot of the chip's own flash while it keeps running; the MCUboot bootloader then swaps it in. No external flash is used.
cc2340r5-ble-dual.boot: The MCUboot bootloader area at the start of flash and a 12 kB settings area at the end are not counted in the image or in the slot. The slot includes a 256 B header and a 152 B signature area that the image figure leaves out.

layouts.name: On-chip, single image with a persistent app
layouts.note: The running app is erased during the download, so a second small app (about 184 kB of flash) stays on the chip to receive the new image. Only TI's stock example was built, not this project's app.

layouts.name: External flash
layouts.note: The new image waits in external SPI flash, so the running image can use almost the whole chip. The repo's notes disagree on whether the LP-EM-CC2340R5 has that flash fitted: oad/README.md says none, and a later map-based note found the pins and a part name from a forum post. Not confirmed on the board.

cc2340r5-ble-dual.pair_note: RAM left is for TI's stock examples. An app that already uses most of the RAM can lose the room: one app with 425 B free was 28 B short of the 453 B the update service needs. The update build is this repo's dual-image example with a blink patch, so it differs slightly from TI's stock build.

cc2340r5-zigbee-ed.layout: Update client on the chip. The end device runs from an image slot, a second slot of the chip's own flash holds the received update, and the MCUboot bootloader installs it. TI pads the end device's update to the second slot's size, so it fits. No external flash is used. The update must also fit the second slot after compression, and the end-to-end update has not completed on the board: twelve transfers from Home Assistant started and the best reached 88.74%.
cc2340r5-zigbee-ed.boot: The MCUboot bootloader area and a 4 kB settings region are not counted in the image or in the slot.
cc2340r5-zigbee-ed.pair_note: The two builds are different TI examples (onoff_light as an end device, and onoff_switch_ota_client_onchip), so the difference in size is more than the update client.
cc2340r5-zigbee-ed.caveat: The room left is not room to grow into: the compressed update must fit the second slot, and the end-to-end update has not completed on the board.

cc2340r5-zigbee-rtr.layout: Update client on the chip, as for the end device, but this role keeps an 8 kB settings region that overlaps the second slot by 4 kB, and its compressed update is larger than the second slot. No router update has been sent: it cannot be signed.
cc2340r5-zigbee-rtr.boot: The MCUboot bootloader area and an 8 kB settings region are not counted in the image or in the slot.
cc2340r5-zigbee-rtr.pair_note: The two builds are different TI examples (onoff_light as a router, and onoff_switch_ota_client_onchip built as a router), so the difference in size is more than the update client.

cc2755p10-ble-dual.layout: Dual image on the chip. The app downloads the new image into a second slot of the chip's own flash and the chip's ROM secure boot installs it. No external flash is used.
cc2755p10-ble-dual.boot: The NVS settings slot is not counted. This chip boots from ROM, so there is no bootloader image to count.

layouts.name: On-chip, single image with a persistent app
layouts.note: The running app is erased during the download, so a second small app stays on the chip to receive the new image. Only TI's stock example was built, not this project's app.

cc2755p10-zigbee-ed.layout: Update client on the chip. The end device runs from a slot of the chip's own flash. Where the downloaded copy waits is not recorded in the repo for this chip.
cc2755p10-zigbee-ed.boot: A 4 kB settings region is not counted in the image or in the slot.
cc2755p10-zigbee-ed.pair_note: The two builds are different TI examples (onoff_switch, and onoff_switch_ota_client_onchip), so the difference in size and RAM is more than the update client.

esp32c6-esphome.layout: ESP-IDF's update layout keeps at least two app partitions in the module's flash and writes the new image to the one that is not running. These ESPHome images were built against one app partition of the size the row names, on the 8 MB module. No external flash is used.
esp32c6-esphome.boot: The bootloader, partition table and settings are not counted.
esp32c6-esphome.doc: Espressif, ESP-IDF Programming Guide, Over The Air Updates (OTA): an update layout needs at least two OTA app slots and an OTA data partition.
